scenarios.hypothesis: A verifier may accept a synthetic credential even when issuer, subject, token class, audience/resource, or lifecycle binding differs from the interface contract.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A deterministic mock verifier compares synthetic issuer, subject, audience/resource, token-class, and generation markers and records only an inert allow-or-deny decision.
scenarios.positive_control: A neighboring synthetic credential issued by the expected mock issuer for the intended subject, verifier, resource, token class, and generation is accepted by the inert oracle.
scenarios.negative_control: A synthetic credential with one deliberately mismatched binding is rejected by the mock verifier while every unrelated fixture dimension remains unchanged.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if validation would expose a real secret, contact a third-party verifier, access production data, or create any irreversible or unauthorized effect.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, every wrong-binding synthetic credential is rejected while the correctly bound neighboring credential remains accepted by the same deterministic mock verifier.
scenarios.credential_origin: The credential originates from a deterministic in-repository mock issuer that emits opaque synthetic fixture identifiers rather than reusable credential material.
scenarios.issuer_identity: The expected issuer identity is a synthetic fixture authority pinned to one deterministic issuer generation and never mapped to a production identity provider.
scenarios.subject_identity: The subject identity is a fake principal dedicated to the fixture, with a neighboring synthetic principal available for one-dimension counterfactual comparison.
scenarios.credential_class: The primary fixture is explicitly classified as a synthetic bearer access token by both issuer and verifier contracts, not inferred from the token string shape.
scenarios.issuance_constraints: Issuance constraints bind the synthetic issuer, subject, intended verifier, audience/resource, limited capability set, fixed test lifetime, and deterministic lifecycle generation.
scenarios.possession_channel: Possession is modeled through a controlled test client that receives only an opaque fixture handle and never exposes or persists a real credential value.
scenarios.storage_representation: Storage uses a temporary synthetic fixture record containing only redacted fingerprints and binding metadata, with no real tokens, keys, or production sessions present.
scenarios.propagation_hop: The credential fixture crosses one controlled mock request boundary where sender, receiver, transport representation, and intended credential class are recorded deterministically.
scenarios.verifier_identity: The verifier identity is a deterministic mock resource service whose expected issuer, token class, audience/resource, and lifecycle generation are pinned in the fixture.
scenarios.verification_decision: The decision trace separately records parsing, semantic class selection, issuer and subject checks, audience/resource validation, generation validation, and the final inert policy result.
scenarios.audience_resource_binding: The credential is bound to one synthetic audience and resource while a neighboring synthetic resource provides the negative counterfactual without touching external systems.
scenarios.represented_authority: Represented authority is limited to one inert fixture capability whose only observable consequence is a deterministic synthetic allow marker rather than a real privileged action.
scenarios.downstream_exchange: No downstream token exchange is required in this scenario; the fixture records that absence explicitly so authority cannot be confused with service ambient privilege.
scenarios.attenuated_effective_authority: Effective authority remains exactly the one inert capability encoded by the fixture and is never expanded by mock-service ambient permissions or unrelated policy state.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a read-only synthetic decision receipt linking credential fixture, verifier identity, resource marker, lifecycle generation, and allow-or-deny outcome.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: The fixture pins a deterministic issuance and verifier generation so the same bindings can be replayed after a controlled generation change without relying on wall-clock timing.
scenarios.revocation_generation: Revocation generation starts at a synthetic baseline and may be advanced in a separate control to confirm the verifier distinguishes current from invalidated lifecycle state.
scenarios.token_class_control: The token-class control substitutes a synthetic identity-token fixture for the access-token fixture while preserving issuer, subject, audience, and test-time state to isolate class enforcement.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Counterfactuals vary exactly one synthetic binding at a time, including subject, audience/resource, verifier identity, token class, or generation while holding all other fixture state constant.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Before promotion, rule out fixture issuer drift, stale verifier cache, deterministic clock mismatch, resource-resolution differences, parser normalization, duplicate delivery, and result-correlation error.
scenarios.evidence_level: The scenario may reach S3 only if the inert mock verifier actually accepts a wrong-context synthetic credential; binding divergence without acceptance remains at S1 or S2.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: The ceiling is S3 for this read-only fixture because it does not create a privileged state change; S4 or S5 requires a separate bounded reversible effect and full lifecycle proof.

scenarios.hypothesis: Credential semantics may change across a controlled propagation hop so that a verifier accepts a synthetic credential as a different token class or across an unintended trust boundary.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled synthetic propagation harness passes opaque fixture identifiers through mock HTTP or RPC metadata and a read-only verifier records class and boundary decisions without external calls.
scenarios.positive_control: The intended synthetic access-token fixture traverses the documented mock propagation path and is accepted only by the verifier configured for that exact class and audience/resource.
scenarios.negative_control: A wrong-class synthetic credential follows the same propagation path but is rejected before any bounded action, while transport and unrelated metadata remain identical.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop if testing would require a live credential, production redirect, real queue, third-party API, credential logging, persistent secret storage, or any non-reversible effect.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, the verifier rejects wrong-class or wrong-boundary synthetic fixtures while preserving the documented propagation of the intended credential class end to end.
scenarios.credential_origin: All credential fixtures are generated by deterministic mock issuers inside the authorized test environment and are represented by opaque non-secret identifiers in captured evidence.
scenarios.issuer_identity: Issuer identity is a synthetic authority pinned in the fixture so propagation changes can be evaluated without ambiguity from multiple identity providers or key generations.
scenarios.subject_identity: A fake principal is bound to the intended credential, with a neighboring synthetic principal used only as a counterfactual and never connected to real account data.
scenarios.credential_class: The primary credential class is a synthetic access token, while identity-token and refresh-token fixtures provide explicit wrong-class controls under the same transport conditions.
scenarios.issuance_constraints: The mock issuer binds class, subject, intended verifier, audience/resource, narrow capability, fixed lifecycle generation, and a deterministic test lifetime to each opaque fixture.
scenarios.possession_channel: The synthetic client possesses only an opaque test handle delivered through the controlled harness, and no actual token string is printed, copied, or stored in evidence artifacts.
scenarios.storage_representation: Intermediate storage is a temporary mock message or request structure containing synthetic metadata and redacted fingerprints, explicitly excluding real secrets and production session material.
scenarios.propagation_hop: The trace records each controlled sender-to-receiver hop, transport field, intended trust boundary, credential-class label, and proof source so semantic drift can be localized precisely.
scenarios.verifier_identity: Each destination is a deterministic read-only mock verifier with one declared credential class and audience/resource contract, allowing neighboring verifiers to serve as safe counterfactuals.
scenarios.verification_decision: The verifier records whether the propagated fixture was classified correctly, whether semantic bindings match the interface contract, and whether the inert policy decision accepted or rejected it.
scenarios.audience_resource_binding: Audience and resource are synthetic labels resolved by the mock verifier, with an adjacent synthetic verifier/resource pair used to test unintended cross-boundary acceptance.
scenarios.represented_authority: Represented authority is a single inert read permission over synthetic fixture data, chosen so an incorrect decision is observable without exposing real data or granting durable privilege.
scenarios.downstream_exchange: No authority expansion is expected during propagation; if a mock exchange occurs, its input and output classes and scopes are recorded and must preserve or attenuate represented authority.
scenarios.attenuated_effective_authority: Effective authority after propagation remains no broader than the synthetic input capability and is compared against the destination verifier contract before any result is emitted.
scenarios.bounded_result: The only result is a deterministic read-only marker or decision receipt correlating source fixture, propagation hop, verifier identity, token class, resource, and outcome.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: A fixed synthetic lifecycle generation keeps propagation tests deterministic and separates token-class behavior from rotation or revocation changes examined in another scenario.
scenarios.revocation_generation: Revocation generation is held constant during class-integrity tests so any accept/reject difference is attributable to token class or propagation boundary rather than lifecycle drift.
scenarios.token_class_control: The core control substitutes identity-token and refresh-token synthetic fixtures for the intended access-token fixture while keeping subject, audience/resource, verifier, and propagation hop fixed.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Counterfactuals change one element at a time: credential class, destination verifier, audience/resource, or propagation representation, while all unrelated synthetic state remains fixed.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Rule out parser normalization, hidden upstream exchange, stale mock verifier state, duplicate delivery, mismatched fixture issuer, alternate resource resolution, and accidental reuse of a prior synthetic case.
scenarios.evidence_level: A class or boundary divergence is S1; convergent verifier context is S2; actual inert wrong-class acceptance is S3; no higher level is claimed without a bounded reversible authority effect.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: This scenario is capped at S3 because its oracle is read-only and inert; higher evidence requires a separate reversible effect plus lifecycle and remediation regression evidence.

scenarios.hypothesis: A controlled downstream credential exchange may broaden synthetic represented authority or continue accepting an invalidated generation after rotation or revocation should have reduced effective authority.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A deterministic mock exchange service and policy simulator emit only synthetic capability sets, generation markers, inert receipts, and reversible owner-controlled fixture state for comparison.
scenarios.positive_control: A properly attenuated same-generation downstream synthetic credential is accepted for its narrow inert capability, and the resulting reversible fixture action produces the expected receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: A broader-than-allowed or invalidated-generation synthetic downstream credential is rejected by the mock verifier while the valid narrow same-generation control remains accepted.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop before any live token exchange, production identity provider, real service account, third-party resource, persistent credential state, destructive action, or unauthorized effect is involved.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, broadened or stale-generation synthetic credentials are rejected, the correctly attenuated current-generation credential still succeeds, and reversible fixture state returns to baseline.
scenarios.credential_origin: The upstream credential originates from a deterministic mock issuer and the downstream credential is produced only by a synthetic exchange service inside the authorized test fixture.
scenarios.issuer_identity: Issuer identities for upstream and exchanged fixtures are synthetic and explicitly pinned so authority changes can be attributed to exchange policy rather than unobserved provider behavior.
scenarios.subject_identity: A fake initiating principal remains correlated across upstream and downstream fixture records, allowing the test to distinguish subject continuity from service-local ambient identity.
scenarios.credential_class: The upstream fixture is a synthetic access token and the downstream fixture is an explicitly exchanged token whose narrower audience/resource and capability set are part of the contract.
scenarios.issuance_constraints: The upstream and downstream fixtures bind synthetic subject, audience/resource, narrow capabilities, exchange permission, fixed issuance generation, and deterministic revocation state.
scenarios.possession_channel: The initiating synthetic client and mock exchange hold only opaque fixture references; captured evidence contains fingerprints and authority metadata rather than reusable secret values.
scenarios.storage_representation: Temporary mock exchange state records synthetic authority sets, generation numbers, and fixture IDs in reversible test storage that is discarded after the deterministic scenario completes.
scenarios.propagation_hop: The authority trace covers initiating client to exchange service to downstream verifier, recording each mock boundary, credential class, audience/resource, and generation transition.
scenarios.verifier_identity: The downstream verifier is a deterministic synthetic resource service configured to accept only the attenuated credential class, current revocation generation, and narrow fixture capability.
scenarios.verification_decision: The downstream decision separately checks exchanged credential class, issuer, subject, audience/resource, current generation, capability set, and policy before producing a reversible fixture result.
scenarios.audience_resource_binding: The exchanged credential is bound to one synthetic downstream verifier/resource, with a neighboring fake resource providing a controlled rejection case for boundary confirmation.
scenarios.represented_authority: Incoming represented authority is a small synthetic capability set that is intentionally broader than the expected downstream subset so attenuation can be measured deterministically.
scenarios.downstream_exchange: The mock exchange converts the upstream fixture into a downstream fixture whose audience/resource and capability set should be narrower and whose lineage points back to the initiating synthetic authority.
scenarios.attenuated_effective_authority: The expected effective authority is the intersection of incoming represented authority and explicit downstream exchange policy, excluding unrelated service ambient privileges.
scenarios.bounded_result: A reversible owner-controlled fixture flag and deterministic receipt demonstrate whether the downstream verifier honored the narrow capability without affecting external or persistent resources.
scenarios.lifecycle_generation: The scenario records upstream issuance generation, downstream exchange generation, and verifier policy generation so rotation and exchange behavior can be separated causally.
scenarios.revocation_generation: A deterministic revocation generation is advanced after a successful baseline, then the same logical synthetic credential lineage is rechecked to prove stale-generation handling independently of expiry.
scenarios.token_class_control: A non-exchanged synthetic access-token fixture is presented to the downstream verifier as a wrong-class control while subject and requested inert operation remain otherwise identical.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Controls compare narrower downstream authority, reduced mock-service ambient privilege, advanced revocation generation, and the remediated flow while holding the initiating subject and inert operation fixed.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Rule out stale introspection cache, deterministic clock mismatch, hidden exchange at another hop, intentionally global service identity, retry duplication, fixture contamination, and incorrect receipt correlation.
scenarios.evidence_level: The scenario may reach S4 when a wrong broadened or stale synthetic credential creates the reversible bounded fixture effect; S5 requires the full causal and remediation controls to pass.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: S5 is permitted only when issuance provenance, verifier trace, class integrity, attenuation, revocation-generation control, alternative-explanation elimination, remediation, and neighboring-flow regression are all directly evidenced.
